changes: v1.3 (2026-10-15, user): Tasks/ with the game's tasks (from Tasks/ on the game repo's orphan tasks branch, never on main; about 10 recommended, at least one), each split into the agent's part and the grader's part, plus a generated Tasks/README.md. v1.2 (2026-10-15, user): the dataset carries the full git history (History/: a git bundle of every commit and every Git LFS object) and the original brief and design doc (Brief/); workflow.jsonl is the record of the person's directions (user.direction rows), no conversation transcripts. v1.1 (2026-10-12): no replay video; ReplayScripts/ only; Dataset.zip next to Dataset/.
description: Our standard delivery layout for every game: the creation record (git.log, workflow.jsonl, ReplayScripts/, the full git history in History/, the brief and design doc in Brief/), the game's tasks in Tasks/, the project, per-scenario gameplay videos, README screenshots and the packaged build. docs/game-format.md is the prose version of this file (v1.1: docs/game-deliverable.md); tools/validate-dataset.ps1 checks against this file.

names.zip_place: the game repo's own folder, next to Dataset/ (git-ignored, with the packager's scratch in .dataset/)

entries.name: README.md
entries.what: game, how to play and open it, how to replay the creation, scenario videos, screenshots, licences

entries.name: git.log
entries.what: every commit, oldest first: message, anonymised author, dates, full text diff; binary and LFS files as path + sha256

entries.name: workflow.jsonl
entries.what: editor operations, one row each, written when the operation happened

entries.name: Brief
entries.what: the original brief the game was built from (brief.md) and the design doc with story bible and status (design.md); images they link may sit next to them

entries.name: History
entries.what: the full git history: <game>.bundle (every commit of every ref except the tasks branch, which never enters the delivered history; scrubbed: anonymised authors, no tool or vendor names) and lfs/objects/<aa>/<bb>/<sha256> (every Git LFS object of every commit, in git's own layout). Restore: git clone <game>.bundle <dir>, copy lfs/ into <dir>/.git/lfs/, git lfs checkout

entries.name: Tasks
entries.what: the game's tasks in the game environment's task format (GameTask, docs/schemas/game-task.schema.json), copied from Tasks/ at the tip of the game repo's orphan tasks branch (never on main) with seed commits mapped to the delivered history: Tasks/<name>/task.json (the agent's part: everything but the grader's) and Tasks/<name>/grader.json (the grader's part: milestones, seed.reference), plus Tasks/README.md (what a task is, the split, the harness rule, how a seed is checked out of History/)

entries.name: UEProject
entries.what: the project at the release commit, with store content; in the repo the repository itself is the project

entries.name: ReplayScripts
entries.what: scripts that replay the creation headless, with Verification/ (report.json with a verdict required for complete; PASS or FAIL is metadata)

entries.name: Gameplay
entries.what: one video per scenario of the release version; may be pending (listed in manifest pending, status pending) while the game has no recordings: a complete delivery has at least one video
entries.scenario_numbers: distinct, 1 or more; a dataset may hold a subset of the game's scenarios (e.g. rally-racer: S2 only, user decision 2026-10-12)

entries.name: Screenshots
entries.what: the README hero and gallery images, linked from README.md by relative path

entries.name: manifest.json
entries.what: metadata and path, bytes, sha256 of every other file

manifest.complete_requires: ReplayScripts/ with Verification/report.json (the creation replay run end to end, headless, from ReplayScripts/ and verified: files outside Content/ byte-identical, assets equal by structure, game maps equal by actors; known non-content differences listed) and manifest.json replay_verification from it; the verdict is metadata (user rule: the replay is required but need not pass): replay_verification.pass equals the report verdict.pass, true or false, and the README says PASS or FAIL
manifest.history_rule: full variant: history is an object (head = commit, the bundle holds every commit, every LFS object of every commit is under History/lfs/objects); repo-dataset: history is null (the repo is its own history)

readme.restore_history_section_repo_dataset: in a repo Dataset/ README the "Restore the git history" section says the repository itself is the history

blocking: the account (user) name of the machine that built it (exact-token allowlist in tools/package-game.ps1)
scan.history: History/: commit messages, author/committer identities (dev_NN only) and every text blob of every commit are scanned the same way
scan.tasks: Tasks/: every text field is scrubbed like the rest of the delivery

unlisted_allowed.why: content-addressed: each file is named by its own sha256 (checked by tools/validate-game.py); manifest.history counts them

workflow.directions: every direction a person gave (what to change and why) is a user.direction row, written before the work it caused; rows acting on it carry "direction": <id>. These rows replace conversation transcripts.

tasks.count: at least 1; about 10 recommended (fewer or more is fine)
tasks.format: GameTask (game-task/1, docs/schemas/game-task.schema.json); merging task.json and grader.json (grader.json's seed into task.json's) gives the task

split.task.json: name, title, instruction, engine, template, seed {game, commit, kind}, play_map, asset_packs, difficulty, tags, limits
split.grader.json: name, seed {reference} when the task has one, milestones

tasks.seed_rules: seed.game = the dataset's game; seed.commit and seed.reference are commits of History/<game>.bundle
tasks.harness_rule: An agent given a task starts from a history-less snapshot of the game at seed.commit with Tasks/, History/ and Dataset/ removed (they hold every task's rubrics and references): only the brief and that snapshot. The grader's half (milestones: rubrics, judge and code-judge questions, log_absent patterns; and seed.reference) never reaches the agent.
